children: Bund yields rose from a two-month low on Monday as oil prices climbed, while investors remained cautious ahead of US midterm elections seen as a key test for global risk sentiment.
German borrowing costs fell in October as a selloff in AI-related stocks drove investors into safe-haven assets while traders reined in bets on European Central Bank rate hikes.

Brent crude futures rose 2% on Tuesday after a report that the United States had struck Iran's Qeshm Island. They had fallen sharply the day before as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials raised hopes for a negotiated way out of the conflict.
Germany’s 10-year government bond yields (DE10YT=RR), the euro area benchmark, were up 2.5 basis points at 3.32%, after hitting 3.2898% on Monday, their lowest level since August 31.
Analysts expect Bunds to remain supported by the prospect of Democratic victories in the US, which could weigh on Wall Street and dampen broader risk appetite.
Polls and independent analysts suggested Democrats were on course to regain control of the House, though the battle for the Senate remained finely balanced.
German 2-year government bond yields (DE2YT=RR), more sensitive to policy rate expectations, rose 1.5 bps to 3.03%.
Euro short-term rate (ESTR) forwards implied a depo rate at 3.16% by late 2027 from the current 2.50% and at 2.72% by December 2026. (EURESTECBM1X2=ICAP)
The yield gap between OATs and Bunds (DE10FR10=RR) was at 162 bps. It hit 177.72 on October 22, the highest level since November 2011.
